title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
technique: exact parallel decoding via Jacobi iteration with lookahead branch generating n-grams and verification branch; no draft model; Lookahead Parallelism across GPUs

optimized_metrics.evidence: Given the pressing need for low latency in various applications, improving autoregressive decoding remains a central challenge.
It allows trading per-step log(FLOPs) to reduce the number of total decoding steps (step compression ratio S)
an exact, parallel decoding algorithm that accelerates LLM decoding without needing auxiliary models or data stores

headline_claim.text: Our implementation of LOOKAHEAD DECODING can speed up autoregressive decoding by up to 1.8x on MT-bench and 4x with strong scaling on multiple GPUs in code completion tasks.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 5-7: tokens/s of single-batch inference and speedup vs autoregressive; Tab 2-3
compression ratio S in Tab 2-3, Fig 8

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define the S = step compression ratio as the number of autoregressive steps divided by the number of LOOKAHEAD DECODING steps to generate the same length of the sequence.
metric_definitions.notes: quote reassembled from two-column text; analogous to mean accepted length per step

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the throughput of single batch inference against these baseline settings
metric_definitions.notes: 'Throughput' = tokens/s of one sequence (batch size 1), i.e. decode speed, not system throughput

load_regime: batch=1 (single-batch inference); discussion notes compute-bound large-batch serving may cause slowdowns
tradeoff_acknowledged: Needs surplus per-step FLOPs; in compute-bound settings (large batch serving) it may slow down; lower speedup on larger models and on GPUs with fewer FLOPs (RTX3090 ~30% vs A100 >50% on MT-Bench). Sampling gives smaller speedups than greedy.
workloads: MT-Bench, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, ClassEval, CNN/DM, XSum
